title: Edge request debouncer, tenant handoff, and fastpath for sustained 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Raval
description:
Summary:
We are seeing recurring tenant-driven 5xx/timeouts during sustained traffic spikes that are amplified by synchronized client retries. This ticket implements an edge-side request debouncer and tenant handoff flow plus a fastpath fast-fail decision so the system can reduce amplification, preserve core capacity, and restore customer-facing latency quickly.

Observed symptoms and context:
- Multiple customers reported ~30-60s periods of 5xx/timeouts from the hosted API during peak bursts (intermittent pattern across regions).
- Traces show large groups of near-simultaneous requests from the same tenant reaching the runtime; many are retries issued by SDKs/clients which then amplify load.
- Existing backpressure and circuit breakers react at the runtime, but by then the serving pools are overloaded and cold-request tails spike.

Goals (success criteria):
1) Reduce retry amplification by at least 65% for affected tenants within the first 120s of a surge (measured by request-rate delta vs sustained capacity).
2) Maintain P95 latency under the SLO for non-throttled tenants during mitigation windows.
3) Provide an observable, auditable handoff path that routes excess requests into a controlled degraded fastpath or snapshot queue that can be drained to Dedicated pools or processed asynchronously.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: edge-level debouncing, tenant-scoped sliding windows, in-flight budget token bucket, handoff to degraded fastpath and snapshot queue, telemetry and runbook updates, SDK guidance for idempotency headers.
- Non-goal: redesign of the runtime kernel scheduler or model-quantization changes (those will be follow-ups if needed).

Design approach (high level):
1) Edge Request Debouncer: lightweight stateful debouncer at the regional edge (L7 proxy) that keeps a short-lived sliding window per tenant+route (configurable 10-60s). If a tenant issues rapid bursts above a threshold, the debouncer will coalesce duplicate requests where possible and apply probabilistic admission for excess identical requests.
2) In-flight Budget Token Bucket: assign each tenant an adaptive in-flight token bucket derived from historical steady-state QPS and recent utilization signals (GPU/CPU P99). Tokens are consumed on request admission; when exhausted, requests are handed to the next step rather than being admitted and causing runtime contention.
3) Fastpath Decision and Snapshot Queue: excess requests that cannot be admitted will be evaluated for a fast-fail vs snapshot pathway. Fast-fail sends immediate structured 5xx/429 with diagnostic headers and guidance; snapshot queue persists request+metadata to a per-tenant queue (short TTL) for later processing to a Dedicated fallback or async worker.
4) SDK and Retry Coordination: add a new idempotency/urgency header recommendation and publish guidance to SDKs to respect the edge fast-fail diagnostic headers and avoid aggressive retries (we will coordinate with SDK team to accept and handle the headers).
5) Telemetry and Automation: instrument new edge metrics (debounce_admissions, debounced_coalesces, token_bucket_hits, handoff_rate) and add alerting for sustained handoff > 10% over 3m. Expose per-tenant timeline in the Console for operators.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Debouncing at the edge reduces immediate runtime load but can obscure per-request signal for some customers — the response headers will include a trace id and explanation to preserve debugging.
- Snapshot queue increases soft storage and introduces eventual processing latency; we will limit snapshot size and TTL to avoid large backlogs.
- Probabilistic admission introduces variance in end-user behavior; experiments will tune the admission curves.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Phase 1 (this ticket, 2 weeks): Edge debouncer prototype, token-bucket admission core, lightweight fast-fail pathway, metrics, and a Canary rollout to one region.
- Phase 2 (follow-up): Snapshot queue persistence and Dedicated fallback integration, SDK header support, Console visibility and per-tenant timeline.

Monitoring and runbook:
- Dashboards: create "Edge Debouncer - Overview" with admission rates, handoff rates, P50/P95 for admitted vs fast-failed.
- Alerts: Alert when handoff_rate > 10% sustained for 3m (priority) or when debouncer coalesce rate > 30% of total in region.
- Runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Edge+Debouncer+Runbook (placeholder)

Rollout and QA:
- Canary region: us-west-2 for 48 hours with synthetic surges (load tests) and one opt-in customer bucket.
- After validation: staged rollout across regions with feature flag gating and kill-switch.

Follow-ups and related work:
- ENG-250210: Snapshot queue consumer and Dedicated fallback glue.
- ENG-101200: SDK header and retry semantics update.
- PM-402: Customer comms + API contract note.

Notes for on-call: when a customer escalates with 5xx/timeouts, check edge debouncer "handoff_rate" and correlate with "runtime_queue_depth" for the tenant. If handoff rate is high and most requests are fast-failed, recommend temporary Dedicated allocation or increasing tenant-tier limits while we analyze traffic pattern.
comments: 2026-03-02: Initial triage call with SRE, Runtime, and SDK teams. Identified synchronized retries from SDK v0.9.4 as an amplifier.
2026-03-03: Prototype debouncer POC completed on dev proxy; coalescing logic reduces duplicate requests by ~72% in synthetic test.
2026-03-04: Security reviewed stateless edge debouncer; no customer data persisted. Security sign-off obtained (secure-ticket-6591).
2026-03-06: Diego Morales pair-reviewed edge admission code. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/784 (draft).
2026-03-08: Added token-bucket backpressure tuning to prototype. Tuned default admission to 0.6*steady_qps to preserve headroom.
2026-03-10: Load test in canary region showing P99 latency improvement for non-affected tenants. Observability gaps noted: per-tenant timeline not yet surfaced in Console.
2026-03-12: Safety flag: need final sign-off from Runtime team on header propagation through internal proxies before rollout. Assigned to @Marta Chen for runtime compatibility check.
Next steps: finalize PR, create canary feature flag, add Console timeline stub, and schedule 48h canary (target start 2026-03-15).
